title: Canonical job lifecycle review draft
description: Declarative contract draft updated with approved decisions. It documents guarded lifecycle and settlement rules only; it implements no queue, worker, persistence migration, feature or provider runtime.

entitySeparation.note: DRAFT and SCRIPT_PENDING_APPROVAL are never generation-job statuses. A failed later generation does not remove an earlier successful project output.

globalInvariants: New admission references an owner-scoped live project and an immutable APPROVED storyboard whose revision/hash and generation settings match the currently selected effective project settings. Settings changes require a new draft and approval; a title-only change does not.

Matching idempotency replay is resolved after authentication/ownership/deletion checks but before new admission checks; it returns the original receipt without another job/reservation even if the worker is now offline or the old job is terminal.
Every new admission reserves one slot regardless of30/60/90 preset; default 3 slots/user/UTC day. Reservation/job/receipt writes are transaction-linked and repeat-safe.

Global capacity is one actually running render job plus up to two waiting jobs. At most one active generation exists per project. A pending cancellation retains its slot/reservation until actual process state is confirmed and terminal settlement is guarded.

Every leased write verifies job ID/current fencing token/lease validity/allowed source state. Heartbeat10 seconds, lease 60 seconds, maximum 2 total automatic execution attempts for the same job/reservation.

Fencing rejects stale writes but cannot stop CPU usage. A worker that loses its lease stops its owned subprocesses; recovery cannot claim a real free render slot merely because a database lease expired.
COMPLETED publication requires both a verified owner-accessible READY clean MP4 and matching selectable WebVTT sidecar. Their shared expiry is verified publication UTC+604800 seconds.
Historical COMPLETED and both artifact IDs remain after media expiry/deletion. Asset metadata/download controls current availability, and every new read/range request checks ownership and revocation.

Publication and cancellation compare-and-set against state/lease/project tombstone: the first committed guarded result wins. Unknown stop/start evidence keeps cancellation pending rather than publishing or releasing resources prematurely.
ExecutionState.renderStartedAt records the first actual RENDER_VIDEO execution and never resets on reclaim. It is internal settlement evidence, not inferred from the current stage alone.

Success consumes the one-slot reservation. System/provider failure releases it. Confirmed cancellation before actual RENDER_VIDEO starts releases it; after any actual render start consumes it, including after a later reclaim. Repeated settlement never double-charges/releases.
Approved narration/settings are never silently rewritten, clipped or sped up. Canonical measured timeline/FPS/dimensions match the approved snapshot.

Narration and caption artifact IDs/hashes/configuration match the canonical timeline. Clean MP4 contains no burned-in caption layer. A separate publication manifest captures final MP4/WebVTT hashes without mutating pre-render inputs.

Successful intermediates clean up after delivery is verified; failed temporary artifacts expire after 24 hours. Final MP4/WebVTT availability lasts 7 days. Hash manifests do not make cleaned/expired blobs available or guarantee byte-identical cross-runtime regeneration.
JSON Schema cannot prove ownership, process termination, asset readiness, hashing correctness, timeline alignment or cross-document transaction integrity.

Late render-start evidence may be recorded while CANCEL_REQUESTED only for an already-started pre-cancel process. It cannot launch/resume work or charge an unauthorized post-cancel launch as earlier user rendering.

New retry of FAILED requires retryable=true; known revision-required snapshots require a corrected new approved draft for any fresh admission. Matching authenticated idempotency receipt replay remains allowed without new work.

leaseExpiredWhileProcessing.action: Reclaim the same generation/reservation under a fresh token at most once, for maximum 2 total execution attempts. Increment attempt; preserve the first actual renderStartedAt and immutable approved input. Revalidate reused artifacts and record new per-attempt execution provenance.
leaseExpiredWhileProcessing.guard: Old worker stops owned subprocesses on lease loss. Coordinator confirms real capacity/process state before replacement execution; state/fencing guards reject stale progress/publication.
deferredDetails: Exact per-stage timeouts await 30/60/90 benchmarks; the current 30-second fixture does not establish 60/90 runtime predictions.

leaseExpiredWhileCancelRequested.action: Adopt cancellation cleanup without restarting narration/rendering or resetting renderStartedAt. Keep CANCEL_REQUESTED/reservation pending while actual process state is uncertain; finalize CANCELLED only after proof of no execution or confirmed termination.

retryAfterTerminalFailureOrCancellation.action: FAILED/CANCELLED user retry creates a NEW generation ID,attempt 0 and new one-slot reservation, linked by retryOf to the original frozen snapshot. Recheck live project/settings approval, owner,3-slot UTC allowance and global1-running/2-waiting capacity. Never mutate old terminal state back to QUEUED; matching idempotent replay still creates nothing.
retryAfterTerminalFailureOrCancellation.failureEligibilityGuard: After an authenticated matching receipt replay is resolved, NEW retry of FAILED requires error.retryable=true. Otherwise reject409 GENERATION_NOT_RETRYABLE. Revision/duration-required failures specifically need a corrected newly reviewed/approved draft; other nonretryable errors require their indicated corrective action. CANCELLED may request new admission subject to normal guards.

completedJobRetry.action: Reject retry with state conflict. A revised approved storyboard is a separate workflow, not retry of a successful job.

terminalCancellation.action: Return409 for already terminal jobs. A still-pending cancellation may acknowledge stored CANCEL_REQUESTED; no acknowledgement claims actual process termination.

canonicalRequestIdentity: concrete projectId or original generationId target
idempotencyContract.sameKeySameIdentity: After auth/ownership/deletion checks, return original admission data receipt before fresh availability/quota checks. Same generationId; no duplicate reservation. Polling reports current state.
idempotencyContract.sameKeyDifferentIdentity: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, including reuse against another target.
idempotencyContract.retention: Separate receipt expiration after 24 hours; retained job history is never TTL-deleted to expire receipts.
deferredDetails: Canonical serializer implementation and post-expiry key treatment must be documented consistently before runtime use; neither authorizes silently changing the owner/action/key namespace.

quotaContract.automaticRecovery: Same job and reservation, up to2 total execution attempts; no new quota.

retentionContract.pairedExpiryRule: clean MP4 and WebVTT expiresAt=the same verifiedPublishedAt UTC+604800 seconds
retentionContract.historicalOutcome: Keep COMPLETED and artifact IDs after expiry/deletion; current asset metadata/read authorization decides availability.
retentionContract.provenance: Retain immutable input/provenance/publication metadata subject to disclosed metadata policy; metadata alone cannot reproduce deleted intermediate blobs.
